name: Fire Warmth
description: Heat sources and the warmth field they radiate: campfires, torches, stoves. Owns fuel burn-down, radius falloff, and extinction — out of fuel, drowned by rain, or stamped out. The field is continuous queryable state sampled per tick rather than enter/exit events, because temperature is a negotiation between every source and the weather at once, and threshold events cannot express 'almost warm enough'. Fire being DANGEROUS (spread, burns) is deliberately not here: world.hazard_volume composed at the same location owns that, because one component that is both comfort and threat cannot be tuned — lowering the burn radius would silently shrink the cozy radius too. Visuals are presentation.particle_system's; this component is the physics of cozy.

inputs.name: baseRadius
inputs.description: Warmth reach at full fuel, in world units. Sized so a campfire warms a shelter's interior but not its roofline — warmth you never have to position is warmth that stops being gameplay.

inputs.name: warmthAtCenter
inputs.description: Degrees of effective temperature contributed at the source, falling off with distance. combat.vital_stats adds this to the ambient reading; it is a contribution, not an override, so two fires genuinely stack.

inputs.name: fuelBurnPerMinute
inputs.description: Fuel units consumed per game minute. Feeding the fire is the loop; a fire that never eats is a radiator, and radiators belong to base stats, not to this component.

inputs.name: rainExtinguishes
inputs.description: Whether exposed fires die in rain via world.weatherChanged. True by default because 'get a roof over the fire' is one of survival's first engineering lessons, and an all-weather fire skips it.

inputs.name: falloffCurve
inputs.description: How warmth decays across the radius: linear, quadratic, or step. Quadratic rewards huddling close; linear rewards room-sized shelters. The curve, not the peak, is where fire placement strategy lives.

outputs.name: isLit
outputs.description: True while burning. An unlit fireplace still occupies the world — it is a promise and a fuel slot, not debris.

outputs.name: fuelRemaining
outputs.description: Fuel units left. At zero the fire goes out on the next tick; the warning radius flicker is presentation's reading of this number, not a separate event.

outputs.name: currentRadius
outputs.description: Effective warmth radius right now, shrinking as fuel runs low. A dying fire pulls the player toward it physically — the field geometry carries the drama.
